property_summary: It is always possible to call Put with zero msg.value (i.e., send 0 wei) and have the contract's recorded Acc[msg.sender].balance remain unchanged while the call succeeds (no revert) and updates unlockTime and emits Log entry — equivalently, Put accepts msg.value==0 without reverting and thus does not require strictly positive value.

For any caller and any put amount/time, after calling Put the contract's recorded unlockTime for that caller is never less than the current block.timestamp (i.e., C sets acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime allows unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs and thus can violate this invariant.

For any Put call, the contract's recorded unlockTime for the caller is always >= block.timestamp (the reference clamps to now), whereas the mutant that directly assigns _unlockTime can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

Reference C guarantees that after Put(...) the stored unlockTime for msg.sender is equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (i.e., never less than the block timestamp unless _unlockTime is in the future), whereas the mutant assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime enabling cases where stored unlockTime < block.timestamp even though _unlockTime < block.timestamp; the test asserts that stored unlockTime >= block.timestamp when Put is called with msg.sender equal to the caller and positive msg.value, which holds for reference but can be violated by the mutant when fuzzing _unlockTime to a past value.

For any caller and any Put(...) call (including zero value), the reference C ensures stored unlockTime for that caller is never decreased below its previous value (i.e., Put only moves unlockTime forward to at least the current block timestamp), while the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can lower unlockTime for some fuzzed _unlockTime, breaking monotonicity.

For any caller and any call to Put(_unlockTime) the reference contract ensures the stored unlockTime after the call is at least the provided previous stored unlockTime or block.timestamp (it never decreases below the prior stored value), while the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can lower (decrease) the stored unlockTime for some fuzzed _unlockTime and thus violate this monotonicity.

After any Put by an account with a positive deposit, the stored unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp if the caller provided a larger _unlockTime (i.e., C preserves a caller-specified future unlockTime when it is greater than now); the mutant resets unlockTime to now breaking that property for some inputs.
